reasons.reader_question: The chapter ends on a hard, specific gap: she is riding into the guild that owns her with a three-day clock, and his warning breaks off mid-word. The question is clear, but it is the obvious one.
reasons.change: Power, knowledge and relationship all move. Raiu is dead, Devan is poisoned on a clock, and Neela leaves the protected position for the guild. Devan also briefly holds the Asha connection and then loses it.
reasons.romance_movement: The reason is new. He now sees her choose risk for him, against her own cage, and he cannot stop her. 'I won't be her... I'm choosing it' moves her from instrument to agent in his eyes.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Care is shown through response, not narration. He noticed the split nail and didn't mention it; she counts on his body; he touches the rough nail and she lets him; his grip fails on her pulse. A little of Neela's interior state is narrated through his POV ('she had gone gentle, and that was worse').
reasons.character_logic: Two weak points. A warden who knows the assassin comes at new-moon dusk walks a stair he has just found deliberately darkened, alone and without a lamp. The poison also erases one specific thought, while the evidence (Raiu's body) stays in the fort for him to see again once he recovers.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Every option costs. Raiu dies partly because of Devan's own 'Hold the head' order. The antidote sits a day away inside the guild, and her three-day sum leaves no slack. Her choice is costly and chosen.
reasons.prose: Lean and concrete, with good lines ('She said it as a sum', 'her mouth went small'), and em dashes stay within limits. The witness-word interiority on the stair is muddled, and a few rhythms repeat ('and she had... and she had... and she had come').
reasons.continuity: No conflicts found. Steps, drain slot, pala rail, newel, Raiu's age and name history, Devan at 26 over Asha, the nails, the blade cut and Muthu's offstage order all match the bible and F331 to F339.

fixes: At 'And the poison put it out. It took the thought as a flood takes a lamp' (Convenient magic / contrived delay): the poison erases exactly one inference, yet Raiu's four-furrow wounds stay in the fort for Devan to see again after the antidote. The plan has him not connect them until book 2. Give the forgetting a rule and remove the evidence by a character's choice. First, have Eravi state, in his sickroom speech, that blackbark gall 'eats the hours before it', a known effect, so the gap is set up rather than convenient. Second, in the stair scene after Raiu dies, have Devan see Neela draw the torn tunic closed and lay her shawl over the furrows before Muthu's lamps arrive, a choice he half-registers and can't read. This keeps F333's fog and plants a later reread of her act. It also stays fair, because Neela knows Vellan's shape and has a motive to cover it.

At 'Not a word. He has not said a word. A man in shape could not speak' (prose / muddled interiority): the paragraph mixes Vellan's silence, Devan's own mouth and the witness rule, so the reader can't tell who must not speak or why it matters. Rewrite it as two clean beats under 60 words. In the first, Devan feels the word 'bear' rise and clamps his teeth on it out of a habit built for her (the pebble). In the second, he realises he never saw the turn, so the word would do nothing to this beast. End on a choice: he does not waste breath on it and moves to the boy.

At 'Devan took the dark stair himself, because it was the only way' (Irrational behaviour to extend plot): he has just found the lamps deliberately drained, and Neela told him Vellan comes at the new moon. A smart Devan reads this as a trap, and 'only way to her door' doesn't justify walking into it unlit. Add one line of chosen reasoning plus one precaution. For example, he takes a hand lamp from the chamber passage, decides he would rather spring the trap himself than leave it for Raiu on his return, and Vellan's first move knocks the lamp down the steps. That turns a lapse into a value-revealing choice (he puts his own body in front instead of his men's), and the fallen lamp can become the 'torch rolling on a step' he later remembers.
reader_question: Will Neela walk back into the Resin House for the antidote, and can she get out before the guild cages her and the poison reaches Devan's heart?
new_facts_assessment: All four new facts are necessary and consistent. F336 (the order is given out of Devan's hearing) is essential: it makes ch26's informant reveal point at Muthu, and it agrees with F244 and F245. F337 justifies Raiu being below the stair and Devan being alone, but it explains the logistics, not the judgement (see fix 3). F338 supersedes F229's 'move only once the bear was gone'; S6 should retire that clause of F229 so the record isn't contradictory. F339 (numbness before the memory loss) is consistent, but it carries more plot weight than it should: the forgetting needs a stated mechanism (see fix 1). One minor point: the poisoned blade smells 'like scorched tamarind', the resin's signature. That is plausible for a blackbark product, but it should stay deliberate, because Devan knows that smell from border school (F041).
